name: SeaweedFS
summary: A distributed storage system that separates volume placement, blob serving, and filesystem metadata while exposing object, file, and lakehouse interfaces.

features.name: Volume, filer, and master separation
features.description: SeaweedFS separates volume servers that hold blobs, a master that tracks volumes and placement, and stateless filer or S3 gateways that provide metadata and client-facing access.
benefits: Keeps file-count metadata out of the master placement service
Allows gateways to scale independently from storage capacity
costs: Metadata-store and placement availability become distinct operational concerns

features.name: Cached direct volume routing
features.description: Clients obtain volume-to-server mappings from the master, cache those mappings, and then access volume servers directly rather than routing blob reads through the master.
benefits: Removes the master from the blob data path
Makes one-blob lookup and read locality explicit
costs: Cached mappings require refresh and invalidation
Placement changes can introduce stale-routing behavior

features.name: Topology-aware replication
features.description: Replication placement can account for racks and data centers, while volume growth, repair, balancing, and erasure coding are explicit maintenance operations.
benefits: Separates foreground writes from selected maintenance work
costs: Replica repair and balancing consume resources asynchronously
Durability depends on placement and maintenance configuration

mathematical_views.question: How do placement metadata, cached volume locations, gateways, and direct blob reads form a graph with a control path distinct from the data path?
assumptions: Volume identifiers map to a bounded set of serving locations
Cached mappings are refreshed when placement changes
Gateway metadata operations are abstracted from blob contents

mathematical_views.question: Under what placement constraints does a volume's replica set tolerate selected rack or data-center failures?
assumptions: Failure domains are represented by the configured topology
A replica is independently readable or repairable
The view abstracts filesystem metadata consistency

benefits: Independent scaling of metadata, gateways, and capacity
costs: More components and cross-service failure modes

benefits: Low-hop blob access and a small placement control path
costs: Routing caches must track topology changes
Copies, repair, and erasure coding require capacity and operational policy
